title: Which nine digit numbers get bigger when any two digits are exchanged?
description: A nine digit number must grow whenever any two of its digits change places. One exchange is studied to see when the number grows, and that rule is applied to every pair of places. The number found is tested with two exchanges.
teaching_notes: One idea: a place on the left is worth more, so an exchange grows the number only when the left digit is the smaller one. Watch for students who forget that equal digits give the same number, and that the first digit cannot be zero.

source: Figure it Out, Q3 (swap and get bigger)
video_script.why: The child knows that places on the left are worth more, and now uses that to decide when an exchange of two digits makes a number bigger.
video_script.substitution: An exchange makes a bigger number only if the left digit is smaller than the right digit; this must hold for every pair of places.
video_script.anchor: a row of nine empty digit boxes for a nine digit number
video_script.payoff_line: The digits rise from left to right and zero is left out

final_answer.spoken: twelve crore thirty four lakh fifty six thousand seven hundred eighty nine, and it is the only such number

maths_rules: exchanging digits d_i (left) and d_j (right) changes the number by (d_j - d_i) x (place value of left - place value of right), which is positive only if d_j > d_i
so each digit is smaller than every digit to its right: strictly increasing, no repeated digit
nine increasing digits chosen from 0 to 9 omit one digit; if 0 is used it is first, which is not allowed, so 0 is omitted
the number is 123456789, written 12,34,56,789 in lakh and crore grouping, and it is the only one
checks: exchanging the first and last digits gives 923456781, bigger; exchanging the first two gives 213456789, bigger
video_script.design: One idea: an exchange helps only when the left digit is smaller, so the digits must rise. The nine boxes stay in the anchor band; the working band builds the rule and the number. No hard clear.
open_questions: The worklist writes the number as 1,23,45,67,89, which is not correct lakh and crore grouping; the correct form is 12,34,56,789. The book answer key says 987654312, which is wrong, because exchanging 9 and 8 makes it smaller.
